featured_reviews.name: RISHABH
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is an outcome and vision of philanthropy and public spiritedness of old school business and something which we don't see nowadays. A hostel built on the ideals of women empowerment and social upliftment, this infrastructure allows a safe and secure residential accommodation in Mumbai for working women. The locality is not that great and safe to be precise and needs overhaul and immediate consideration by the local authorities. Although the locality of the hostel is a middle income area but the approach road and the adjacent place of the hostel is not safe for females because drunk local play cards and drink alcohol just outside the hostel although they are not an active threat, yet potential danger looms if your office working hours are late. The hostel is gated and manned by hostel staff and generally safe. The hostel has basic creature comfort and needs improvement, but are yet to get a filtered RO water purifier for the residents. Food served is not healthy at all and its nutritional value is poor the reason often given is the low price charged but the hostel is anyways a not for profit organisation and serving poor quality and quantity food in 2023 in a developing economy by a charitable institution run by one of India's largest corporate puts question on the overall management. Summarising the entire review, for potential residents they have a good place in Mumbai and it gives you a family safe place to grow financially in India's most expensive city at the same time the management needs to improve the infrastructure and use its CSR funds to overhaul and upgrade the hostel and make the residents feel like home, empowered and not that they are  at the mercy of some corporate magnate as it would be anthesis to the real value, philosophy and objectives of the Birla and ideals of Rajashreeji Birla.
